interest: Shows State Department vetting of a suspect Shanghai firm via trade directories, then referring the case to Naval Intelligence, 1939.
overview: 1939 Far Eastern Affairs memos on suspect Takahashi: an unlisted Shanghai firm couldn't be verified in trade directories, so the case was referred to postal authorities and the Office of Naval Intelligence.

people.name: J. E. S.
people.role: Officer, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: M. M. H.
people.role: Official, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Recommends awaiting further postal reports and sharing information on Takahashi with the Office of Naval Intelligence.
subfiles.summary: J.E.S. finds evidence on Takahashi insufficient for action, recommending a postal report and referral to Naval Intelligence.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by J.E.S. recommending liaison with ONI concerning Takahashi

subfiles.about: Transmits a request for a recommendation on action regarding the Takahashi file.
subfiles.summary: Brief 1939 inter-office note from M.M.H. asking J.W.B. for a recommendation on the Takahashi case.
subfiles.title: Routing slip from M.M.H. requesting recommendation on action

subfiles.about: Reports that the Chinese Import and Export Company of Shanghai cannot be identified in standard commercial directories.
subfiles.summary: J.E.S. reports the Chinese Import and Export Company of Shanghai could not be verified in standard trade registries.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by J.E.S. on Chinese Import and Export Company of Shanghai
